issue.body:
While checking `gulp-eslint` unit tests against eslint@1.9.0, I found that the "fix" option failed to correct the second (earlier in code) of two fixable messages; though, this test would pass prior to 1.9.0. You can find the failing test [here](https://github.com/adametry/gulp-eslint/blob/412098fe32dda7e4adf34c360ec3744e9ddcad25/test/linting.js#L228), or as described below.
#### CLI-Config

``` javascript
{fix: true, rules: {'no-extra-semi': 1, 'no-trailing-spaces': 2}}
```
#### JS Source

``` javascript
var x = 0;; 
```

_Note that there is an extra space after the second comma_
#### Expected Fixed Output

``` javascript
var x = 0;
```

_Note that the trailing space and second semi-colon have been removed_
#### Actual Fixed Output:

``` javascript
var x = 0;;
```

_Note that only the trailing space has been removed_

After stepping through the ESLint code, I found that the change #4329 resulted in an off-by-one flaw. Specifically, `fix.range[1]` is an exclusive upper boundary, while `lastFixPos` is an inclusive lower boundary from the previous fix. When the opposing bounds are equal, the two boundaries do not overlap; rather, they are adjacent.

_eslint v1.9.0 (via gulp-eslint@1.1.0)_

issue.body:
[`no-extra-semi`](http://eslint.org/docs/rules/no-extra-semi) fix only removes one extra semicolon.

eslint@1.10.3

Input:

``` js
var test;;;;;
```

Output:

``` js
var test;;;;
```

Expected output:

``` js
var test;
```
